problems.field: studies[S1].participants.n_randomized (null) and its rationale in participants.exclusions, eligibility.reason, and reconciliation.agreed_fields_checked
problems.form_value: null, with the rationale 'The exclusions came after assignment. ... The paper gives no per-cell breakdown of the 12 exclusions and no count at assignment.'
problems.source_says: The paper's own accounting implies that 224 people were assigned. All 224 recruited people took part: 212 were analyzed, and the 12 exclusions arose in the session (10 failed condition-check items about their own partner and AI condition, 1 facilitator error with the session handout, 1 participant who had trouble writing her ideas). 224 - 12 = 212, so there is no other loss. The form itself says all 12 exclusions came after assignment, and that contradicts 'no count at assignment'. The paper never calls 224 the number assigned, and its random-assignment sentence prints the post-exclusion cell counts (sum 212). For this reason null is defensible under the form-spec rule. The timing is explicit only for the 10 condition-check failures. For the other 2 it is an inference from the handout (given in the session, after the teammate was announced on arrival) and from the written ideas. Fix: record study n_randomized = 224 marked as inferred, or keep null and replace 'no count at assignment' with 'the assigned count is implied (224) but not stated; the assignment sentence prints post-exclusion counts'. The arm-level nulls are right. No recorded count changes, and criterion 2 is unaffected. The c094 people challenge flagged the same pattern.
problems.quote: A total of 224 participants were recruited for this in-person lab experiment ... Two participants were also excluded from the study: one due to a facilitator error in failing to provide the required written handout

confirmed.statement: S1 analyzed 212 people. The abstract, Section 4, Section 4.1, and Table 2 all give N = 212, and the paper prints no other analyzed total.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4.1 ('The final sample consisted of 212 undergraduate students'); p. 1, Abstract; p. 4, Section 4; p. 9, Table 2

confirmed.statement: The arm counts match the paper: Independent/human 69 (HHT), AI-assisted/human 68 (AI-HHT), Independent/AI 37 (HAT), AI-assisted/AI 38 (AI-HAT). They sum to 212, which gives 106 per ideation condition and 137 vs 75 per teammate condition. The form's arm labels match the cell names in Fig. 1 and Hypotheses 3a-3b.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4 (Method); p. 4, Hypotheses 3a-3b; p. 9, Fig. 1

confirmed.statement: The cell counts are the analyzed people, although the paper prints them in its random-assignment sentence. Every main-effect and interaction test has F(1, 208), and 208 = 212 - 4. The simple effects have df 135 = 137 - 2 and 73 = 75 - 2. From the cell ns and the printed cell means and SDs, I reproduced the three printed 95% CIs ([.32, .68], [.24, .67], [-.72, -.16]) and all six simple-effect F values within rounding.

Table 1 marginal means and Table 2 overall means equal the averages of the Section 5.3 cell means weighted by 69/68/37/38, within rounding (originality: independent 2.99, AI-assisted 3.347 vs 3.34 printed, human 3.238, AI 3.041; overall 3.168 vs 3.17). Table 1 prints no ns.

The counts are people, not ideas or ratings. Each participant's idea ratings are averaged to one score, and quantity and flexibility are counted per participant, so each ANOVA has one row per person. The gender shares reproduce from 212 people (160, 50, and 2 give 75.5, 23.6, and .9 percent). counts_are = people and n_units = null are right.

The attrition in the form matches the paper: 224 recruited, 10 excluded for failing condition-check items, 1 for a facilitator error, 1 for a language barrier, 212 analyzed. No page gives exclusions by cell. The paper has no flow diagram (Fig. 1 is a design schematic without counts). So the arm-level n_randomized = null is right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4.1; p. 9, Fig. 1 and Table 1; whole document read (PDF pp. 1-10 and the full markdown, appendix included)

confirmed.statement: The paper reports one study. Data were collected in two semesters and coded in two periods, but they are analyzed as one sample of 212. The paper names no other study or paper that uses these participants. It says only that the study was nested within a larger project.

No other paper in the screening reuses these participants. candidates.json has no other Dai and van Swol record (c276 is by a different Dai). A web search found only a UW-Madison Communication Arts news item dated December 1, 2025. It describes the two-stage project (individual ideation, then human-human or human-AI pairs) and gives no counts and no other publication. The blank shares_participants_with is right. A later paper on the pair stage would share this sample.

The form's participants quote is verbatim. The who, country, and population fields match the text: undergraduates, one extra course credit, a $20 gift card for the top 25 percent, and University of Wisconsin-Madison IRB approval no. 2025-0106.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4.1; p. 8, Exemption statement

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds on S1 alone: 212 people analyzed, 106 per AI condition. It also holds inside each anticipated-teammate group (137 and 75 people). This matters because the teammate factor was set by arrival, not at random.

summary: The form's analyzed counts are right and count people: one study of 212 undergraduates (69 HHT, 68 AI-HHT, 37 HAT, 38 AI-HAT, so 106 per AI condition) after 12 in-session exclusions from 224 recruited, and every ANOVA df, the three printed CIs, and the Table 1-2 means reproduce from these counts, with no participants shared with another known paper. The one defect is minor: study-level n_randomized is null because 'no count at assignment' is given, although the form itself says all 12 exclusions came after assignment (which implies 224 assigned), and criterion 2 holds by a wide margin (212 analyzed, and 137 and 75 inside each teammate group).
